storedTranscript.text: Hello, and welcome! こんにちは。I'm Ryota, your English teacher today. In this lesson we'll talk about your work and a project you're involved in, and practise the present perfect and the past simple. Does that sound good to you?
I'm ready.

Great, let's begin. First, a short, friendly chat so I can see what you can already do. Please answer in English, and don't worry about mistakes.

Can you tell me a little about your job? What do you do?

Yes, I'm sales manager and the G I'm our uh the GM uh general manager, well, that's and I just supporting for the old division in the the company. And of course, most of the current of the management and the sales area for this.
Thank you. So you manage the sales team and support the division. What kind of products does your division sell?

My main responsibility in sales area to the contact for the clients and supporting for the each division member about this. And of course, I have a suggesting for the uh the new uh products about to the clients.
Thank you for explaining your role. Have you ever worked with an international customer? If so, can you tell me about the experience?
I have worked with international customer sometimes.
Good, thank you. Which countries were those customers from?
I'm not sure about it.
No problem. Let me ask it more simply: which country were your customers from? For example, the United States, China, or Thailand?
Yes.
Sorry, I'm not sure I understood. Which country were your customers from? 例えば、アメリカ、中国、タイなど、どの国ですか。
Yes, I have been working a project with uh uh us from another content, another uh countries.

Thank you, that's a good start. You are working on a project with customers from other countries, so we will use that. Today we'll focus on making your sentences about experience more accurate and natural.

Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
and lady.
Sorry, I didn't catch that.
I'm ready.

Good, let's start. We'll talk about your work and responsibilities.

For experience that continues now, we say "I have worked with international customers for three years." For a finished event at a specific time, we say "I worked with an international customer yesterday."

Now, what are your main responsibilities at work? Please answer with at least two sentences.
My responsibility in sales area is uh contact for our clients and supporting for the EDF member and suggesting for the new product clients.

You explained your role clearly. One point to fix: after "responsible for," we use the -ing form of the verb. You said "contact," so the sentence should be "I am responsible for contacting our clients." Can you say that sentence?

My main responsibility in the sales area is to be a contact for our clients, supporting for the each division member of of course the management for the each division member and of course uh suggesting for the new service and the project products to the clients.

Your answer shows your main responsibilities clearly. This time the key form, "responsible for" plus -ing, did not appear, so here is the correct version: "My main responsibility is contacting our clients and supporting my team."

That completes our work on talking about your job. Next, we'll practise the present perfect for experience that continues now.

We use the present perfect (have or has, plus the past participle) for experience that started in the past and continues now. For example: "I have worked here for five years."

Have you worked for your current company for a long time?
Yes. for our company above over the 10 years.
Not quite. You said "for our company over the 10 years," but the sentence needs the present perfect verb. Please say the full answer with "have worked" in it.
I have here over the 10 years.
Could you say the full answer once more? Start with "I have worked for our company..." and tell me how long.
I have working for our company for a long time. It takes about uh around the 10 years.

Your meaning is clear, and you have worked for the company for about 10 years. The one error is "have working"; after "have" we use the past participle, "worked." So the full sentence is:

 I have worked for our company for about 10 years.

That completes the present perfect. Next is the past simple, for things you did at a specific time in the past. Shall we go on to it, or do you have a question first?
Yes.

Let's go on. We use the past simple for things that finished at a specific time in the past.

For example, "I attended an exhibition last year."

Did you attend any business events or exhibitions last year? Answer in English, using the past simple.
Yes, I attended the uh some business event in the uh Japan. last year.

You used "attended" correctly, because "last year" is a specific time in the past. One small thing: we say "some business events" without "the". The corrected sentence is:

 I attended some business events in Japan last year.

What was the event about, and what did you do there?
Uh, it's kind of the networking events, uh, the looking for the new uh business partner or the connecting for the the related our service.

Networking events are a good way to find new business partners. One small thing: we say "connect our services with related companies." Now let's have a more natural conversation about your work.

What is one project you've worked on that you're particularly proud of? Try starting with "I worked on a project to..."
I worked on a project to support SNS networking content.
That's a clear sentence, and "worked on a project" is the right past simple form. What was your role in the project, and what did you do?
Ah, my role is to manage for the member who is making for the content uh, the talking about for the content. and making for the content.
Good, you explained your role clearly. One point: we say "manage the team members," with no "for." Can you say the full sentence once more?
I need to manage
My role is to manage for the assessment and networking content member.
Not quite. The verb "manage" goes straight to its object, so there is no "for" after it. Can you say the sentence again, starting with "My role is to manage..."?
Take your time. Try starting with "My role is to manage…", then say who you manage.
Uh, I think in the future, I will supporting for the the global networking to the between the foreigner company and the Japanese company with my uh our directors.
Not quite. After "will," we use the base verb, so "supporting" becomes "support." Can you say the sentence once more with that change?
one more again.
Sure, let's try once more. Start with "In the future, I will..." and tell me what you will support.
Uh, not project, but I have to find for the the new uh person to exchanging for the the uh the project members.
Thanks for trying. I'm not sure I understood the end of your sentence. Did you mean, "I have to find a new person to work with the project members"?
Uh, because of is we're leaving to our company and the project going on, so that's why I have to find a new people.

Thank you, that explains it clearly. You are leaving the company, the project is continuing, so you need to find a new person. A more natural way to say it is:

 I have to find a new person because I am leaving the company, and the project is continuing.

Could you say that sentence once?

Uh, what I have the long at the my company, it uh connecting to the foreigner person because of a company, a lot of the foreigner and uh I have to using for my English to communicate for the each other.

Your meaning is clear: many foreign people work with you, so you need English. The one thing to fix is "have to," which is followed by the base verb, "use," not "using."

Can you say that sentence once more?
Yes, I have working with the international customer for sometimes.

Your sentence shows that you have experience with international customers, and you explained your role clearly in this lesson. The one thing to fix is "have," which is followed by "worked," not "working." Please say this sentence once more.

Today you described your job, a project and your experience. Your past simple sentence about the business event was clear and correct. Next time, please practise the present perfect with "have worked" and the -ing form after "responsible for."

Thank you for today's lesson, and well done! Keep practising these grammar points when you talk about your work.
